_meta.provenance: Crop optimal-temperature bands and key-disease conditions are compiled and cross-checked from published agronomic and plant-pathology sources (ICAR / ICRISAT / TNAU Agritech / IMD Mausam, plus standard extension and peer-reviewed references), cited per crop in `sources`. These are the load-bearing, advice-driving numbers and are treated as verified.
_meta.humidity_model: Humidity is deliberately NOT a generic per-crop 'comfort band' — humidity risk is crop- and growth-stage-specific, so it is expressed through DISEASE SUSCEPTIBILITY: each crop's key disease has a temperature+humidity favouring rule AND `susceptible_stages` (the growth stages when that disease actually damages the crop). The Crop Watch response says WHY (which stage, which disease, what humidity/temperature) rather than a blanket 'humidity > 90% is bad'.

verified.soil_moisture_opt: APPROXIMATE — Open-Meteo volumetric water content (m3/m3), derived from soil-physics norms (wilting point ~0.12, field capacity ~0.30-0.40 for loam). ICAR schedules irrigation by IW/CPE ratio or crop coefficients, NOT an optimal m3/m3, so this band is an engineering approximation, not an ICAR citation.

units.temp_opt: degrees Celsius (comparable to live air temperature)
units.stage_days: approximate total crop duration in days
units.key_disease.favors.humidity_min/max: % relative humidity threshold that favours the disease (min = humid-favoured, max = dry-favoured)
units.key_disease.susceptible_stages: growth stages (of Germination/Vegetative/Flowering/Yield Formation/Maturity) when the disease is most damaging

_meta.note: Before the final demo a domain teammate should still sanity-check these against their local ICAR/GKMS package of practices; the file is structured for a data-only edit.

sources: TNAU Agritech, Crop Production :: Wheat (ideal 10-15C winter / 21-26C spring) https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/agri_cropproduction_wheat.html
Stripe rust favoured by cool (8-16C) + humid/dew, tillering-to-flowering (ICAR-IIWBR)
Rice optimum ~20-35C, best 25-30C (IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank)
Blast: 25-28C / RH >=89% + leaf wetness; leaf blast (veg) + neck blast (heading) (UC IPM; IRRI) https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/rice/rice-blast/
Maize optimum ~20-30C
Turcicum leaf blight favoured 18-27C + RH >=90% / leaf wetness (J. Plant Dis. Prot.) https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41348-016-0054-8
Cotton optimum ~21-30C
Leaf-curl virus/whitefly favoured by hot (30-35C), moderate-low RH (~64-66%); early-stage infection most damaging (Arch. Phytopath. Plant Prot.) https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340024103
Soybean optimum ~20-30C (best 26-30C)
Rust favoured 16-28C + RH >75-90% with leaf wetness; flowering-podfill (UNL CropWatch; UMN) https://cropwatch.unl.edu/plant-disease/soybean/soybean-rust/
Groundnut growing optimum ~20-30C
Tikka (Cercospora) leaf spot favoured 25-31C + RH >85% for ~3 days (IMD Mausam; TNAU eagri) https://mausamjournal.imd.gov.in/index.php/MAUSAM/article/download/949/790/3408
Rapeseed-mustard optimum ~10-25C, dry at flowering
Alternaria blight favoured max 27-28C / min 14-15C, RH >65-85%; flowering-siliqua (Sci. Reports) https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-022-10108-z
Chickpea optimum ~18-30C (veg 20-25C), cool-season Rabi
Botrytis grey mould favoured 20-25C + high humidity/cloudy at flowering & podding (ICRISAT) https://oar.icrisat.org/2301/1/Botrytis_grey..management.pdf
Field pea prefers cool 10-18C, declines >25C at flowering (TNAU eagri AGR 301) http://eagri.org/eagri50/AGRO301/lec07.html
Powdery mildew favoured by warm dry days + cool dewy nights, moderate humidity; flowering onward (WSU Hortsense)
Potato best 15-25C (tuberization 15-20C)
Late blight: congenial temp ~7.2-26.6C + RH >=90% (ICAR JHULSACAST model, Potato Journal) https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/PotatoJ/article/view/50164
Tomato ideal 21-27C, poor set >32C
Early/late blight favoured moderate temp (16-26C) + RH >=90% / leaf wetness (UMN Extension; UC IPM) https://extension.umn.edu/disease-management/early-blight-tomato-and-potato
Lentil optimum ~18-30C (cooler veg), heat-sensitive at flowering
Rust favoured by mild 20-25C + high humidity around flowering/podding (GRDC Lentil ute guide) http://lentils.grdc.com.au/lentils/lentil-rust

high_temp.title: Protect the crop from heat stress
items: Irrigate in the cooler evening to bring canopy temperature down
Avoid spraying or fertiliser during the midday heat
Mulch to conserve soil moisture

low_temp.title: Guard against cold / frost
items: Irrigate before a forecast cold night — moist soil holds heat
Delay any planned sowing while a cold spell is expected
Cover young seedlings where feasible

low_soil_moisture.title: Low soil moisture in the root zone
items: Irrigate to bring the root zone back to its comfort range
Mulch to slow further drying
Hold off nitrogen until moisture recovers

high_soil_moisture.title: Root zone is waterlogged
items: Clear and improve field drainage
Pause irrigation
Watch for root and collar rot

disease.title: Watch for {disease}
items: Scout for early symptoms of {disease} at this growth stage
Prepare a preventive spray if these conditions persist
Avoid overhead irrigation that keeps the canopy wet

heavy_rain.title: Heavy rain expected
items: Make sure drainage channels are clear
Delay spraying and fertiliser until after the rain
Support lodging-prone crops where possible

comfortable.title: Conditions look favourable
items: Continue your routine irrigation and monitoring
Maintain the nutrient schedule
Keep scouting for early pest or disease signs
